correctness.rationale: A direct 16-element character-sum formula proves the finite real-even flat sign with no appeal to an existence theorem. All nonzero normalized coefficients equal plus or minus 1/4. Tensorization and the order-four cosine/sine transform yield one survivor per antipodal pair. For each level j the perturbation variation equals a/(2*4^j), the positive comparison density has separating expectation gap a^2/2, and the fourth Fourier-power mass equals a^4/16^j. Summable variation builds a finite mass-one measure dominated by a singular product. Exact Fourier-factorization proves full support E; finite E intersection (gamma-E) plus polar approximation proves strong small-2 for arbitrary complex spectral measures. Parseval yields the displayed finite convolution-square L2 norm. The included exact Gaussian-integer checker verifies all 17,472 coefficients for j=1..3; the analytic proof covers all j.

originality.rationale: The new object is the pure exponent-four product, obtained from an explicit reversible flat sign on the order-four square. Ohrysko 2026 supplies the general mechanism but realizes its examples only on exponent-six and odd-prime-exponent products. Those groups cannot be reindexed to the exponent-four group, and the new real-even order-four flat sign is an additional finite ingredient not supplied by the original examples. Direct and alias searches and comparison with the available prior statements found no equivalent exponent-four theorem; unindexed prior constructions remain a risk.

value.rationale: The object is the first nontrivial pure 2-primary exponent after the Walsh exponent-two antipodal obstruction. The result constructs a strongly small-2 but non-Riesz spectrum on the pure exponent-four compact product, rather than transferring an odd-order factor or improving an arbitrary numerical parameter. It adds a concrete reversible 16-point flat sign to a published general mechanism and gives an explicit singular full-support witness with exact L2 convolution-square norm. It is a motivated group-structure boundary and a meaningful new existence case, not a claimed classification of all such spectral sets.
